title: Seven days of silence
hookLine: his friends sit silent with him seven days, their finest hour (Job 2:13)

lines: A SLOW LINE AT A WAKE.
cards: At a wake, a slow line of people moves past the family. Each one leans in and says something. I'm so sorry.
She was a lovely woman. Call me if you need anything. Then somebody reaches the front, takes a hand in both of theirs, and says nothing at all.
Just holds on, stays a moment, and moves along. Saying nothing can be the hardest thing in that line to do. In the book of Job, three friends do exactly that, and for a long time.

teach.b: First, they come. Three of Job's friends, Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar, hear of everything that has fallen on him.

Each sets out from his own place; they had made an appointment together "to come to mourn with him and to comfort him." Before a word is said, they make a plan, and they travel. Second, they don't know him.
From far off they look up and can't recognize their friend. So they raise their voices and weep. Each tears his robe.
They throw dust into the air, over their heads, toward heaven. Their mourning is loud and physical before it's anything else. Third, they sit down.

teach.h: THEY SIT ON THE GROUND WITH HIM.
teach.b: "So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great." Upon the ground, with him, at his level, not standing over him.
Day and night, and nobody fills the air.
Fourth, silence that comes from seeing. The verse gives one reason for the quiet: they saw how great the grief was.
Some readers take it that words would have been too small for it. Some call this the friends' finest hour, partly because of what happens when they finally open their mouths. But that's tomorrow.
For now: they came, they wept, they sat on the ground where he was, and they kept quiet because they could see.

how: Some Jewish and Christian readers take Job 2:11–13 as a picture of comforting mourners; in Jewish mourning custom, visitors come to sit with the bereaved, and tradition has visitors wait for the mourner to speak first.

games.q: you're one of Job's friends. you've traveled to him and found him on the ash heap, hard to recognize. what do you do?
o: tell him why this might have happened
remind him that things will get better
sit down on the ground with him and say nothing
games.why: they sat down with him upon the ground and none spake a word, for they saw that his grief was very great.

practice: Settle down low if you can, feet flat or even on the floor, and bring to mind someone who is hurting right now.

In your mind, go and sit next to them on the ground, at their level, and say nothing: no advice, no reasons, no it'll be okay. If words come up, let them pass like a car outside, and keep seeing them.

wordCard.voice: Eliphaz, one of Job's three friends who sat with him on the ground seven days and nights without a word, because they saw his grief. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: sit with them. Sometimes the quiet, kept close, is the comfort. Until tomorrow.
